question: Should `gateway.controlUi.allowedOrigins` allow scheme-level wildcard entries such as `chrome-extension://*`, and what exact wildcard grammar is acceptable for Gateway browser-origin authorization?
rationale: The requested behavior broadens which browser origins can reach Gateway HTTP/WebSocket handling, and current docs intentionally limit this config to full origins plus the global `*` allow-all policy.

options.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
options.body: Define a small explicit wildcard grammar, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document allow/reject cases before accepting the feature.

options.title: Keep exact origins only
options.body: Reject scheme wildcards and rely on exact opaque-origin fixes plus the existing global `*` escape hatch for intentionally broad testing.

options.title: Defer to broader origin-pattern design
options.body: Wait for loopback origin-pattern work to settle, then decide whether extension scheme wildcards belong in that same contract or a separate one.

recommendation.title: Approve constrained scheme wildcards
recommendation.body: Define a small explicit wildcard grammar, implement it in the shared origin helper, and document allow/reject cases before accepting the feature.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history on the current Gateway origin-check boundary and its security hardening.
